title: The story catalog carries 2,534 dependency rows while the story files carry 2,609 for the same 1,034 stories
source: Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1, Dependencies sheet; the story files behind _work/msr/fragments for the ten stories named
description: The Dependencies sheet of the Service Story Catalog v1 has 2,534 rows (H 1,600, C 440, I 412, X 82). The story files of the same run carry 2,609 rows for the same 1,034 stories (H 1,664, C 451, I 412, X 82), so 75 rows exist in the story files and not in the catalog, and none exist in the catalog that the story files lack. The 75 belong to ten stories: RWB-P3-AD019-APP, RWB-P3-E2006-APP, RWB-P3-E2007-APP, RWB-P3-E2009-APP, RWB-P3-E2013-APP, RWB-PLT-E1027-APP, RWB-PLT-E1037-APP, RWB-PLT-E1042-APP, RWB-PLT-E1043-APP and RWB-PLT-N009-APP. 64 are H rows to the template contracts DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 plus the story's own CON, and 11 are C rows from platform stories to the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision contracts. The catalog keeps the material dependencies only.
evidence: Service Story Catalog v1 Dependencies sheet: 2,534 rows. _work/msr/fragments: 2,609 rows over the same 1,034 story ids. Row-set difference: 75 rows (64 H, 11 C), 0 rows the other way; ten stories affected.
proposed: Use the catalog as the source of the v5 graph and state the template baseline once on the Dependency classes sheet; the story files keep their rows and no story is re-cut.

title: Five of the 325 story dependencies of version 4 are carried by no row of the realigned graph
source: Recovery Workbench Dependency Map v4, Story dependencies sheet; Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1, Dependencies sheet
description: Five version 4 story dependencies have no v5 row in any class between the new stories of the two legacy stories. RWB-E1-056 to RWB-E1-007, to RWB-E1-015 and to RWB-E1-069: RWB-E1-056 became RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS, a DevOps story, and it carries no dependency row at all. RWB-TE-009 to RWB-TE-004: RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG carries no row and RWB-TE-004 became RWB-PLT-TE004-APP and RWB-ITG-TE004-ITG. RWB-TE-010 to RWB-TE-003: RWB-ITG-TE010-ITG carries no row and RWB-TE-003 became RWB-PLT-TE003-APP and RWB-PLT-TE003-APP-2. All five are team-type work outside the application lane.
evidence: Legacy dependency trace sheet: 325 rows, 5 with Status Not carried. Story dependencies v5 has no row between any slice of the pair. The other 320 are carried: 312 directly and 8 through the R6 redirect or a retired story.
proposed: Keep the five rows visible in the trace as Not carried: an OPS story and two QA harness stories start on Day 1 from the platform template. A follow-up adds an X row if the run books or the harness really waits for the named story.

title: Ten class X rows point at a platform application story rather than at a DB, INF or OPS story
source: Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1, Dependencies and Stories sheets; Template and Rules R5.4
description: Template and Rules R5.4 defines X as external or team-type work, naming a DB, INF or OPS story of the same legacy key or an outside system. Ten rows use X for platform technical-enabler work whose work type is App development. Five application stories depend on RWB-PLT-TE012-APP (document storage containers): RWB-P1-E1017-APP, RWB-P5-E1024-APP, RWB-P5-E1049-APP, RWB-P5-E1057-APP and RWB-P5-E2017-APP. Five platform stories depend on RWB-PLT-TE001-APP (recovery module folder and boundary test): RWB-PLT-E1071-APP, RWB-PLT-TE002-APP, RWB-PLT-TE003-APP, RWB-PLT-TE011-APP and RWB-PLT-TE012-APP. H is not available because the target is neither the same service nor a CON story, and C needs a CON story, so X is the only class that keeps the row outside the blocking set.
evidence: Story dependencies v5: 82 X rows, of which 10 point at an App development story (74 inside the same service, 8 to platform work). Dependency classes sheet, check row X.
proposed: Keep X on the ten rows and record the reading on the Dependency classes sheet: platform technical-enabler work is team-type work, so it is tracked and never blocks.

title: Five of the six Wave 0 platform dependencies of Architecture v5 slide 39 have no row in the external dependency table
source: Recovery Workbench Dependency Map v4, Dependencies sheet; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slide 39
section: Dependencies sheet note rows; Dependency classes
description: Architecture v5 slide 39 names six decisions needed from the architecture team. DEP-04 covers the ACE common contracts (sign-in, notification path, shared case view adapter, restructure calculator, audit and PII logging) and DEP-36 covers the approval of the Temporal and Drools versions. The other five have no row in DEP-01 to DEP-36: the Kafka hosting of the business-event topics with ACLs separate from PII logging; the 19 schemas and 19 logins on the ACE PostgreSQL server with a connection budget per service; the shared Temporal layer with one namespace per workbench and 1.30+ for Nexus; the decision ledger model; and the BOT approval route under FPG 19/2560 cl. 5.5. Slide 39 states that the first three are needed before Wave 0 starts.
evidence: Dependencies sheet: DEP-01 to DEP-36, owners and decisions. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 39 (six decisions with owners) and slide 38 (Wave 0 enablers).
owner_role: ACE team with Enterprise Architecture; Platform team; Risk and Internal Audit; Compliance and IT Risk
proposed: Record the five on the Dependency classes sheet exactly as slide 39 states them and create no new DEP ID in this version; the next version of the Risks Assumptions Issues and Dependencies document takes them as DEP-37 to DEP-41 with the slide 39 owner roles.

title: 124 non-CON stories carry no dependency row, 31 of them application stories
source: Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1, Stories and Dependencies sheets
description: Of the 1,034 stories, 622 carry at least one dependency row. Of the 412 that carry none, 288 are CON stories, which correctly have no build dependency (Template and Rules R5.7 rule 1). The other 124 are non-CON: 57 DevOps, 31 App development, 18 Infrastructure, 11 ACE DB and 7 Integration. The OPS, INF and DB stories are the other team types' own work and the 7 ITG stories are harness stories. The 31 application stories take only the template-baseline contracts, so the catalog lists no row for them.
evidence: Service Story Catalog v1: 1,034 stories, 622 with a row, 288 CON stories, 124 non-CON stories without a row (57 DevOps, 31 App development, 18 Infrastructure, 11 ACE DB, 7 Integration). All 939 Day 1 stories are in the catalog as Day 1.
proposed: Publish the template baseline rule once on the Dependency classes sheet and keep the 31 application stories at Day 1; a story that turns out to have a real in-lane dependency gets the row in its own story file first, then in the next version of this map.
